title: Coherent composition of finite-coefficient pullback on strict systems
statement:
Let $A_1\leftarrow A_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be an inverse sequence of finite commutative rings and ring homomorphisms. Let $j:Y\to Z$, $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be arbitrary morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use fixed small representatives of their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $B_{T,n}=(A_n)_T$ for the constant ring sheaf and use its canonical inverse-image identifications, compatible with maps of coefficient rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. For each scheme $T$ let $\mathscr S_T$ be the abelian category of sequences of $B_{T,n}$-module sheaves $M_n$ with $B_{T,n+1}$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{T,n+1}\to B_{T,n}}M_n$; morphisms commute with these maps and exactness is componentwise [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\mathscr S_T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For each composite $f$ of the given scheme maps let $U_f:D(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{target}(f)})\to D(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{source}(f)})$ be the functor obtained by applying the exact finite-coefficient module inverse image levelwise and then termwise to complexes [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

The canonical module-pullback composition maps determine natural isomorphisms of derived-system functors
$$a_{h,k}:U_{k\circ h}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_hU_k.$$
For every complex of strict systems, this is represented by the termwise module comparison at every degree and coefficient level; these module comparisons commute with the semilinear transitions. Evaluation at level $n$ identifies $a_{h,k}$ with the canonical finite-coefficient derived comparison $c_{h,k}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. For every $S\in D(\mathscr S_V)$,
$$U_j(a_{h,k}(S))\circ a_{j,k\circ h}(S)=a_{j,h}(U_kS)\circ a_{h\circ j,k}(S)$$
as morphisms in $D(\mathscr S_Y)$, under the canonical associator. This equality is induced by an equality of natural transformations on complexes of strict systems before localization. No normalization, boundedness, constructibility or flatness of $A_m\to A_n$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, proof: termwise composition on flat-term K-flat representatives. The varying-coefficient strict-system comparison, transition compatibility and its associativity equation are the agent-formulated refinement extracted from the integral pullback composition argument; 0D6D alone does not assert them.

proof.text: Write $P_f$ for the underived levelwise pullback. For a coefficient homomorphism $r:A_{n+1}\to A_n$, the square $c^f_{A_n}\circ f^{-1}(r)=r\circ c^f_{A_{n+1}}$ commutes: after adjunction both maps send a constant section $a$ to the constant section $r(a)$, and uniqueness of extension from the constant presheaf proves equality. Thus inverse image of an $r$-semilinear map is $r$-semilinear after the canonical ring identifications. For composites, [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition] identifies the canonical structure map with the composite structure map. This checks that all the single-level module adjunctions below use exactly the coefficient maps stipulated in the statement.

source.place: Tags 03D3 and 03D7, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules and lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; constant-section specialization using the defining sheafification

proof.text: On a strict system $M$, set $(P_fM)_n=f_n^*M_n$, with transition the inverse image of $\tau^M_n:M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}M_n$. Define $(R_fN)_n=f_{*,n}N_n$, its transition by applying the underlying sheaf direct image to $\tau^N_n$, with scalar action through the canonical coefficient map. The coefficient square in Step 1, after taking its adjoint, is the direct-image identity\n\(f_*(r_X)\circ\rho^f_{A_{n+1}}=\rho^f_{A_n}\circ r_Y\); hence applying \(f_*\) to \(\tau^N_n\) is\n\(B_{T,n+1}\)-linear into the restricted target, so these are valid system transitions. For a family $s_n:f_n^*M_n\to N_n$, its componentwise adjoint is $t_n=f_*s_n\circ\eta_{f,M_n}$. The system equation $\tau^N_n s_{n+1}=s_n f^{-1}(\tau^M_n)$ is equivalent under the underlying sheaf adjunction to $f_*(\tau^N_n)t_{n+1}=t_n\tau^M_n$: substitute the formula for $t_n$ and use naturality of $\eta_f$; the inverse implication uses the inverse adjunction bijection. The module adjunction and its underlying-sheaf formula are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport]. Hence they restrict to $P_f\dashv R_f$ on strict systems, with componentwise units. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] and componentwise exactness in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], $P_f$ is exact.

source.place: Tags 03D3 and 03D7, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules and lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; restrict the componentwise Hom bijections to transition-compatible families

proof.text: For $f:T\to T'$ and $g:T'\to T''$, define $d_{f,g}:R_{g f}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_gR_f$ levelwise by the canonical identification of direct images. On an object $Q\to T''$ it is induced by $(Q\times_{T''}T')\times_{T'}T\cong Q\times_{T''}T$. This is the direct-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Restriction of sections along this scheme isomorphism commutes with every sheaf morphism, in particular the semilinear transitions; it preserves scalar multiplication since the scalar maps send each constant to the same constant. Thus $d$ is an isomorphism of system functors. For three maps the two fibre-product identifications have identical projections to $Q$ and the final source scheme, hence are equal by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Applying sheaves and restriction gives the right-adjoint associativity equation, as an equality of maps of whole strict systems.

source.place: Tag 03D8, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; expand the direct-image formula and fibre-product universal property

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to $P_fP_g\dashv R_gR_f$, $P_{g f}\dashv R_{g f}$ and $d_{f,g}$. Let $b_{f,g}:P_{g f}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_fP_g$ be the inverse of the resulting unit-compatible isomorphism. It is a map of systems by construction. Evaluate its unit equation at $n$: all units and $d$ evaluate to the ordinary level-$n$ units and direct-image comparison from Steps 2 and 3. Uniqueness in the same conjugate-isomorphism lemma identifies $(b_{f,g,M})_n$ with the canonical module comparison of [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition]. In particular those specified module comparisons, and their inverses, commute with the semilinear transitions; this is obtained before deriving, not by an equality test in the derived coefficient categories.

source.place: Tag 03D8, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; categories.tex Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, unit characterization

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-adjoint-composition-coherence] with categories $\mathscr S_V,\mathscr S_W,\mathscr S_Z,\mathscr S_Y$, the six adjunctions of Step 2 and the right-adjoint comparisons of Step 3. Its coherence hypothesis holds by the projection calculation in Step 3, with the canonical associators retained. Its conclusion is the equality for the unit-compatible maps $b^{-1}$. Invert that equality and use functoriality to obtain
$$P_j(b_{h,k,M})\circ b_{j,k h,M}=b_{j,h,P_kM}\circ b_{h j,k,M}.$$
This is an equality of natural transformations between functors on the abelian categories of strict systems.

Apply $P_f$ degreewise to complexes. Naturality of $b$ with respect to each differential makes its components chain maps, and its inverse is degreewise a chain map too. Thus $b$ gives a natural isomorphism on complexes of strict systems. The equality in Step 5 holds at every degree as an equality of system maps, so it is an equality of natural transformations on these complex categories. Exactness of $P_f$ and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] give exactly $U_f$, computed termwise on every complex. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) to the natural isomorphism $Qb$ to obtain $a_{f,g}$. Its compatibility with composition and clause (3) transport the equality from complexes to the stated equality in $D(\mathscr S_Y)$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; natural-transformation descent uses Mathlib CategoryTheory.Localization.liftNatTrans and natTrans_ext as recorded by the cited localization node

proof.text: Exact evaluation $e_n$ is termwise on complexes and derived categories by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. It therefore carries $a_{h,k}$ to the localization of the canonical termwise module comparison of Step 4. To identify this with the specified $c_{h,k}$, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. On that resolution [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] represents $c_{h,k}$ by precisely this termwise comparison. All three finite-coefficient pullbacks are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]; hence their termwise functors preserve the resolution quasi-isomorphism, and naturality carries the same identification to every complex. This identifies the natural comparisons under the canonical exact/derived functor identifications. The construction never tensors a transition along $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, so it requires no coefficient-flatness; it applies to arbitrary complexes and arbitrary strict systems.
